slides.0.title: Level 2 final assessment
slides.0.subtitle: Rules, four sub-regions, winemaking and producers
slides.1.title: Level 2 review: rules and classification
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOC skeleton
slides.1.highlights.0.content: White or rosé sparkling wine, second fermentation in glass bottle; seven principal varieties plus the trial variety Voltis; whole-bunch harvest, no irrigation
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Yield and pressing
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Base 12,400, ceiling 15,500 and reserve 10,000 kg/ha; one 4,000 kg pressing gives at most 2,550 L (2,050 cuvée plus 500 taille); the Comité Champagne sets the marketable yield each year
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Échelle des Crus
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Village-based: Grand Cru 100%, Premier Cru 90–99%, others 80–89%; the current INAO list has 17 Grand Cru plus 42 Premier-Cru-only villages, all in the Marne; the end dates (2004/2010) and 42/44 are source discrepancies
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Ageing rules
slides.1.highlights.3.content: From tirage: NV 15 months, Vintage 36 months; disgorgement not before 12 months; Vintage ≤ 80% of the year's wine with no reserve wine
slides.1.content: Numbers with source discrepancies are outside the assessment: Premier Cru 42/44, the end date of the price scale, Aube area and variety shares, producer counts and yearly marketable yields.
slides.2.title: Level 2 review: the four sub-regions
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Montagne de Reims
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Pinot Noir dominates; nine Grand Crus (Ambonnay, Beaumont-sur-Vesle, Bouzy, Louvois, Mailly-Champagne, Puisieulx, Sillery, Verzenay, Verzy); Villers-Marmery and Trépail lean to Chardonnay; Coteaux Champenois reds
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vallée de la Marne
slides.2.highlights.1.content: More Meunier towards the west; two Grand Crus (Aÿ, Tours-sur-Marne); the Vallée de la Marne pruning is for Meunier only
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Côte des Blancs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Chardonnay on chalk; six Grand Crus (Avize, Chouilly, Cramant, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Oger, Oiry); variety limits for Grand Cru villages are not current rules
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Côte des Bar and outer areas
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Aube, Pinot Noir dominant, Kimmeridgian marl, no Grand or Premier Cru; Les Riceys and Rosé des Riceys (Pinot Noir only); Côte de Sézanne and Montgueux lean to Chardonnay
slides.2.content: 17 = 9 + 2 + 6; the Aube has none.
slides.3.title: Level 2 review: winemaking and the industry
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Winemaking I
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Whole-bunch pressing, cuvée/taille fractions, débourbage, first fermentation (MLF optional, no wood pieces) and blending (with reserve wines)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Winemaking II
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Tirage (from 1 January), second fermentation in bottle (5–6 bar), lees ageing and autolysis, remuage, dégorgement and dosage (Brut Nature <3 to Doux >50 g/L)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Styles and producers
slides.3.highlights.2.content: NV, Vintage, Blanc de Blancs, Blanc de Noirs and Rosé; the NM/RM/CM division of labour; Prestige is a market term
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Industry governance
slides.3.highlights.3.content: The Comité Champagne, built from SGV and UMC, sets the marketable yield each summer; still wines fall under two AOCs, Coteaux Champenois and Rosé des Riceys
slides.3.content: After this you can move to Level 3: viticulture in depth, style essays, regulation and markets.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 📋 Level 2 final assessment
Under the INAO specification, what are the minimum months from tirage for NV and Vintage?
NV 15 months and Vintage 36 months, both from the tirage date.
How are the 17 Grand Crus distributed across the Montagne de Reims, Vallée de la Marne and Côte des Blancs, in that order?
Montagne de Reims 9, Vallée de la Marne 2 and Côte des Blancs 6 make 17.
For one 4,000 kg marc, what are the volumes of cuvée and taille?
Which statement about Vintage Champagne is correct?
A. It may contain up to 20% reserve wine
B. It needs only 15 months of ageing
C. It comes entirely from one year and is capped at 80% of the operator's wine of that year
D. It must be Blanc de Blancs
Vintage has no reserve wine, at least 36 months of ageing and an 80% cap.
Who decides the marketable yield each year?
D. Each house on its own
The Comité Champagne decides each summer; the specification only sets the base and ceiling.
On the price scale, what were the percentages for Grand Cru and Premier Cru?
Grand Cru 100%, Premier Cru 90–99% and other villages 80–89%.
Which statement about the Côte des Bar (Aube) is correct?
A. Chardonnay dominates and it has three Grand Crus
C. Pinot Noir dominates and it has no Grand or Premier Cru villages
D. It lies completely outside the Champagne AOC
Pinot Noir dominates the Côte des Bar, and all 17 + 42 listed villages are in the Marne.
For which variety does the specification restrict the Vallée de la Marne pruning?
Specification: this pruning technique is authorised for Meunier only.
How soon after tirage may disgorgement occur under the specification?
Disgorgement may not take place before 12 months after tirage.
Which variety is used for Rosé des Riceys?
INAO specification: Pinot Noir only, still rosé.
What do the label codes NM, RM and CM stand for?
NM is a house (négociant-manipulant), RM a grower-producer (récoltant-manipulant) and CM a cooperative.
